statutoryAuthority.ruleStatement: An individual may move to vacate and expunge a prior Class 4 felony prostitution conviction after completing every sentence or condition imposed. The motion is filed with the circuit court with jurisdiction over the underlying conviction, its Chief Judge, or a judge designated by the Chief Judge. The State's Attorney has 60 days after notice to object with supporting evidence, and the court decides the motion under the discretionary standard recorded for this route.
doNotImport: Do not map or import the statewide cannabis form suite; no statewide form suite exists for this route, and a published local form controls where one exists.

Do not assert that the conviction was a Class 4 felony where the record does not say so, predict success, compose the participant's adverse-consequences narrative, or characterize the circumstances of the offense.
Do not add verification language; 20 ILCS 2630/5.2(j)(3) requires none.
Do not use this route when the participant's involvement resulted from trafficking; the stronger 20 ILCS 2630/5.2(h) route requires different questioning.

documents.title: Motion to Vacate and Expunge Conviction for Class 4 Felony Prostitution Under 20 ILCS 2630/5.2(j)(3)

sections.heading: Motion and grounds
sections.body: The movant asks under 20 ILCS 2630/5.2(j)(3) to vacate and expunge the prior Class 4 felony prostitution conviction identified from the court record. The participant supplies the conviction date and exact wording, the date every sentence and condition was completed, and the participant's own adverse-consequences statement. The packet does not assert the classification, compose the narrative, characterize the offense circumstances, or predict success.

sections.heading: Relief requested
sections.body: The motion asks the court to vacate the conviction and order expungement in the manner provided by 20 ILCS 2630/5.2(d)(9)(A), with the effect provided by 20 ILCS 2630/5.2(j)(8). It states that the State's Attorney may object within 60 days after notice.

documents.title: Proposed Order (Tendered for the Court's Consideration)

sections.heading: Tendered order
sections.body: The proposed order is tendered for the court's consideration, identifies the conviction in the participant's copied record wording, and would direct vacatur and expungement under 20 ILCS 2630/5.2(d)(9)(A) only if and when a judge signs it. Every judicial decision and signature field remains blank.

participantChecklist.text: Stop before using this packet if your involvement resulted from trafficking; the stronger 20 ILCS 2630/5.2(h) route requires different questioning.
Confirm from the record itself that the conviction is clearly worded as a Class 4 felony prostitution conviction; do not let the packet or memory supply the classification.
Obtain the Illinois State Police statewide criminal history transcript through Access and Review.
Obtain documentation from the circuit clerk or probation department that every sentence and condition imposed by the conviction is complete.
On the motion, copy the county, existing case number, conviction date, exact conviction wording, and completion date from the records, never from memory.
Write the statement of the specific problems the conviction has caused in your own words; the packet composes none of it.
On the proposed order, copy the same county, existing case number, and exact conviction wording used on the motion.
Sign and date the motion personally. No verification or notarization is required by this subsection.

Ask the circuit clerk whether a published local form controls, how to file, whether a county fee applies, and what local copy or cover requirements apply; use the Supreme Court Rule 298 waiver application if a fee applies and you cannot pay it.
Ask the circuit clerk whether the clerk or the movant handles notice to the State's Attorney, and follow the clerk's local direction.
File the completed motion and proposed order in the existing criminal case with the circuit court identified by the approved route record.
